# `project_onboarding` — version 1.1

Source: `presets/project-onboarding.satz`

## Purpose

The projects on the estate, one entry of `projects` each. Per entry a Google project
with its own IaC service account and state bucket, and the interface that publishes
them to the project.

A project is an estate beside this one, in its own repository, that reads this estate
through `interfaces/<name>/`. Onboarding one is an entry in `projects`,
`{ name = "payments" owner_group = "payments-owners@example.com" }` — bound in the
estate, or requested by the project as `contributes_projects` in a small pack of its own,
checked with `satz check-request` and vendored into the estate by pull request. The
entry's `name` is the interface's name and a folder name: lowercase letters, digits and
`-`, starting with a letter. Its `owner_group` is the group's address, `<name>@<domain>`.
The request point's patterns refuse either at compile, naming the entry and the value.

PER ENTRY. The Google project `{customer_shortname}-<name>-001`, billed to the
infrastructure billing account, with the five APIs a project's estate needs to run.
Its IaC service account `svc-iac-<name>`, which holds the project's IAM and its
services and the state bucket `{customer_shortname}-<name>-001-state` — what the
project's own estate grants itself the rest from (`satz update-prerequisites` there).
The owner group reads the project and may become its IaC service account, that account
only. `interface "<name>"` publishes `project_id` (an attach point for
`google_project_iam_member`), `project_number`, `iac_account` and `state_bucket`;
`satz init --project <name> --interface interfaces/<name>/<name>/satz/interface.satz`
writes the project's estate from them and the core export `default_region`.

WHERE THE PROJECTS GO. `project_onboarding_folder` names the parent: empty is the
organisation; the workload folder `satz init --workload-folder-name` writes is
`google_folder.workload_folder.name`.

MORE IN AN INTERFACE. An interface declared in two files is one interface, so the estate
adds to a project's interface by writing a block of the same name in its own file:
`interface "payments" { use interface "network" }`.

NO CLAIM. The projects are workloads, not controls: this pack witnesses nothing.

## Use it

```
params {
  use_project_onboarding = true

  // the pack's own defaults — copy only the lines you change
  projects = []
  project_onboarding_folder = ""
}

use "presets/project-onboarding.satz" when use_project_onboarding
```

`use_project_onboarding` is the gate: while it is falsy the pack contributes nothing — no resources, no params, no claims. It is declared by `estate_map`, and the estate's own binding wins.

**Needs from outside the pack:**

- `billing_account_infra` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `customer_shortname` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `default_region` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.

## Questions

What to ask before this pack is configured, and what changing the answer costs.

| asks about | prompt | reversal | blast | recommends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_onboarding_folder` | The folder the projects are created in — the workload folder as `google_folder.workload_folder.name`, another folder the estate declares as `google_folder.<label>.name`, an existing one by its numeric id, or empty for the organisation | edit | low | — |

**project_onboarding_folder** — It decides the policies and the grants every project inherits. Changing it afterwards moves every live project between parents.


## Contributes

| resource type | labels |
|---|---|
| `google_project` | `one per entry of projects, by name` |

## Exports

Outputs of the root module and values of the interfaces under `interfaces/` in every estate that uses this pack: a `core` export is carried by every interface, another one by its own interface and every interface that uses it. An interface a pack declares is common: every project's folder carries it.

| interface | output | value | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{each.name}` | `project_id` | `"${google_project.{each.name}.project_id}"` | The project's Google project — attach point for `google_project_iam_member` |
| `{each.name}` | `project_number` | `"${google_project.{each.name}.number}"` | Its number, looked up |
| `{each.name}` | `iac_account` | `"${google_service_account.{each.name}_iac.email}"` | The IaC service account the project's estate runs as |
| `{each.name}` | `state_bucket` | `"${google_storage_bucket.{each.name}_state.name}"` | The bucket the project's estate keeps its state in |

`{each.name}` is written once per entry of `projects`, named by the entry's `name`, and each is one project's own interface, not a common one.

## Requests

What a project may add to this pack's lists, through `contributes_<param>` in a file the estate uses after a reviewed pull request; `satz check-request` checks such a file.

| list | key | fields | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `projects` | `name` | `name` matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, `owner_group` matching `[^@: ]+@[^@: ]+` | A project on the estate: its name, which is its interface's, and the address of the group that owns it |
